Description

Are you a creative and inventive engineer who loves to understand how things work?
Are you interested in reverse engineering and exploiting software and hardware devices?

We are seeking motivated developers, computer scientists, computer engineers, and cyber researchers who are passionate about advancing the field of cybersecurity! The Systems Exploitation team performs vulnerability research, develops novel cyber capabilities, and pioneers groundbreaking approaches to defeat sophisticated security protections.

As an intern in the Systems Exploitation group, you may...

- Exploit hardware, firmware, and software
- Reverse engineer embedded systems
- Collaborate with teammates to identify vulnerabilities or security weaknesses stemming from publicly disclosed information or previously unknown vulnerabilities
- Aid in the development of proof-of-concept capabilities or extend existing capabilities
- Explore techniques for automating binary analysis and reverse engineering
- Learn from experts in software development, reverse engineering, and vulnerability analysis

Interns typically work as part of a larger team and are given tasking scoped to match the duration of their stay. At the end of the internship, each intern prepares a short presentation highlighting their work and project contributions.

Qualifications

You meet our minimum qualifications if you are...

- Pursing a Bachelor's degree, Master's degree, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline.
- Maintaining a minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale
- Proficient with programming languages such as C, C++, Python, Rust
- Familiar with reverse engineering tools, software debuggers, and/or static analysis tools (Ghidra, IDA Pro, Binary Ninja, Windbg, gdb, etc)
- Comfortable with Linux/Unix operating systems
- Familiar with one or more assembly languages (x86/x64, ARM, MIPS, etc.)
- Able to obtain an Interim Secret level security clearance by your start date and ultimately a final TS/SCI Clearance. If selected, you will be subject to a government security clearance investigation and must meet the requirements for access to classified information. Eligibility requirements include U.S. citizenship.

You will go above and beyond if you are also familiar with…

- Basic exploitation techniques such as buffer overflows and command injections
- Experience with Capture the Flag exercises and/or hackathons
- Windows, Linux, Android, and/or iOS internals
- Cross compiling toolchains for embedded devices
- Experience with hardware design or development (e.g., digital circuits, FPGAs, or embedded systems)
- Familiarity with hardware interfaces and protocols such as I²C, SPI, and JTAG
- Experience working with RF systems (e.g., wireless communications, software-defined radio, or RF debugging tools)
- Symbolic execution engines such as angr

- Software engineering

- Network security

- Operating system security

- Secure/Authenticated boot

- Incident response and adversary detection

- Vulnerability research

- Build prototypes and help identify, design, and test security improvements

- Further our mission of providing secure and reliable Internet to underserved communities

- Bachelor's degree in computer science or another STEM discipline

- Experience with one or more software development languages (i.e. Python, C++, Golang)

- Graduating in the class of 2026 or 2027

- Designing secure systems

- Experience contributing security improvements to complex systems

- Experience working with special purpose security hardware such as Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) and Hardware Security Modules (HSMs)

- Experienced in navigating large, complex, interactive systems

- Flexibility, communicating clearly, and establishing and maintaining productive working relationships with other engineering teams

- Ability to work both independently and in a team

- Demonstrated ability to deal with ambiguity and to learn new technologies quickly

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our products combine complex digital logic, high-speed interfaces, embedded control, and test infrastructure to deliver reliable connectivity across demanding systems.

The opportunity

Join the Design-for-Test (DFT) team and help make complex silicon easier to test, debug, and manufacture. You’ll learn how DFT structures and methodologies are designed, implemented, verified, and analyzed across the chip development flow.

This internship is designed for someone who enjoys connecting digital design fundamentals with practical silicon-quality challenges. You’ll work with experienced engineers on a meaningful project involving test structures, patterns, coverage, simulation, or debug, while collaborating with RTL design, physical design, verification, validation, and manufacturing-test teams.

What you’ll do

- Learn the product domain, DFT flow, project goals, development environment, and processes needed to contribute effectively.

- Support DFT architecture and implementation activities for digital designs, including scan, test compression, memory test, built-in self-test, boundary scan, JTAG, and design-for-debug structures.

- Work with RTL, netlists, constraints, test modes, clocking, resets, and power intent as needed to understand and implement test requirements.

- Generate, run, and analyze structural test or ATPG patterns and investigate coverage, fault, rule, or simulation results.

- Support scan insertion, test-logic validation, MBIST/BIST configuration, test-mode checks, or related DFT flow activities under engineering guidance.

- Run simulations and, where applicable, gate-level or X-propagation checks to debug DFT behavior and identify unexpected or uninitialized signals.

- Analyze logs, reports, waveforms, coverage results, and pattern failures to identify root causes and recommend next steps.

- Develop or improve scripts and automation for DFT setup, pattern generation, regression execution, report parsing, or result analysis.

- Collaborate with RTL, verification, physical design, silicon, validation, and manufacturing-test teams to communicate issues and track corrective actions.

- Participate in code and flow reviews, technical discussions, issue tracking, documentation, and project planning.

- Deliver assigned DFT work in a usable state and explain what was implemented, verified, or improved and how it supports the product flow.

- Present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.

What you bring

- Coursework, projects, research, or hands-on experience in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related field.

- Foundational understanding of digital logic, RTL, computer architecture, semiconductor design, or hardware verification.

- Programming or scripting experience in one or more of Verilog, SystemVerilog, Python, Tcl, Perl, C, C++, or a comparable language.

- Curiosity about how chips are tested and debugged and a methodical approach to analyzing technical evidence.

- Comfort learning in a Linux environment and working with command-line tools, source control, and technical documentation.

- Ability to organize priorities, ask focused questions, communicate progress and blockers, and follow through on commitments.

- Self-motivation, learning agility, professionalism, and a collaborative mindset.

Helpful experience

- Scan chains, scan compression, ATPG, fault models, fault coverage, pattern generation, or test-point insertion.

- MBIST, BIST, boundary scan, JTAG, IEEE 1149.1, design-for-debug, or manufacturing-test concepts.

- Verilog/SystemVerilog RTL simulation, gate-level simulation, assertions, lint, or X-propagation analysis.

- DFT or EDA tools, test-mode configuration, clock observation, reset architecture, or power-aware verification.

- Python, Tcl, Perl, or shell scripting for automation, report parsing, regressions, or data analysis.

- PCIe, CXL, Ethernet, SERDES, retimers, SoC design, or other high-speed connectivity technologies.

- Git, Jira, Confluence, or similar collaborative engineering workflows.

Internship experience and compensation

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship.
